POL-C3-LA-05 (SAARC): four directions for the look

Each option is shown at the same three moments of Part 1, built from the real clips, the presenter and the map data. Nothing in the delivered video has changed. Pick one (or mix: say which parts of which) and the whole video is rebuilt in that look.

Now: गोल मेज़

What was delivered, for comparison.

  • Procedural walnut wood reads as ripples, not a table.
  • Clips are small circles inside a heavy maroon disc.
  • Many small cream tags of different sizes; brass plates and rings crowd the frame.

A · शिखर रात (summit night)

Cinematic documentary. A dark summit hall, footage as a wide film still that fades into the dark, one gold accent.

  • Background: deep blue-black with a soft spotlight behind him.
  • Clips: full width, about half the screen, fading into the background. No frame.
  • Text: large white lower-thirds; one gold pill for the takeaway; points as a thin 5-segment bar.
  • Map: dark land, gold coastline, glowing pins.

Serious and premium; the footage gets the most room of the framed options.

B · रंगीन explainer (bright flat)

A clean, bright ed-tech explainer. Each of the five points gets its own colour, and that colour follows him.

  • Background: light grey-blue with a faint dot grid.
  • Clips: a big rounded photo card with a white border and a colour number badge.
  • Text: chunky rounded type on white chips; the point colour marks the takeaway; a coloured disc behind him.
  • Map: flat light map, numbered colour chips per country.

The most readable on a phone; colour-coding helps the five points stick.

C · पूरा पर्दा (full-bleed reel)

Reel-native. The clip fills the whole screen; he stands in front of it; words hit hard in white and yellow.

  • Background: the footage itself, with dark gradients top and bottom.
  • Clips: full screen, every time; blurred clip behind the point cards.
  • Text: huge kinetic words, red strike-throughs, yellow highlight blocks; Instagram-style progress bar.
  • Map: white coastline over a blurred crowd, yellow name tags.

The most energetic, and it uses the Veo clips the most. He covers part of the footage.

D · नक्शे पर (the atlas is the stage)

South Asia itself is the background for the whole video. Clips are postcards taped onto the map; points are collected as stamps.

  • Background: a teal-and-sand atlas of the region, always there.
  • Clips: postcards with tape, slightly tilted, over the map.
  • Text: serif ribbons like an atlas cartouche; a wax-seal number; five postage stamps fill with each point's picture.
  • Map: it is the background; pins drop on it.

The most specific to SAARC, and the map stays in view all the way through.

Mock-ups are stills, so motion is not shown: transitions, the iris/slide of pictures, and how text arrives would follow the chosen direction. The words, timing, clips and sound stay as they are.
